# R409 — Native AVX2 CPU decode kernel candidates for IQ3_S GU / Down

Date: 2026-10-13 (Asia/Tokyo). Status: source-only, external primary-source review. No source edits, builds, tests, lint, AST checks, GPU/profiler work, process/service inspection, cleanup or Git mutation were performed. The concurrent serialized Main diagnostic was not inspected or touched. No throughput improvement is claimed.

## Question and limits

Look for selective IQ3_S GU and Down kernel changes that could improve native CPU decode throughput on a Ryzen 5 5600X, and compare the current source with primary GGML/llama.cpp implementations. This report separates code-path observations from measurements. The current ledger D is source-only and only adds caller/layer route accounting; it is not evidence of CPU job execution, physical DRAM/H2D traffic or request critical path. Do not call CPU service the decode bottleneck from that ledger. The current decode target is raw spec=4, NT=1; first decode begins with the final prompt token. The requested long decode benchmark is unchanged `upstream bench.sh --long --runs 3` with the actual 32,049-token prompt. No such run was performed here.

## Local source identity

Canonical worktree supplied for this pass: `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/feat-restore-layer-major-prefill-20261013`, stated base `4951d2be7b674bb688832bf0b3cb750410f1a432`.

The IQ source files match prior frozen-source receipts: `iq_avx2.cpp` and `iq_avx2_rows.inl` have the R371 v2 fingerprints. Current `native_expert.cpp` and `pool.cpp` were read to confirm dispatch; `pool.cpp` SHA-256 is `c114539980d496ea69c17fee2ddaf1b7229668afe07586142f572d96cb8a7036`.

## Current local behavior and relevant prior evidence

`iq_avx2.cpp` implements scalar IQ3_S decoding (`Fmt32<21>`) and gathered decoding (`Fmt32<121>`). The scalar path builds eight indices and gathers grid entries with scalar indexed loads; the gather path builds eight indices in AVX2 lanes and uses `i32gather`. `iq256_variant_for` auto-selects gather only for type 21 when the CPU-local `cpu_gather_fast_here()` says it is fast. Existing comments document Intel P-core gains and regressions across other Intel core classes; there is no measured 5600X result in those comments. `STRATA_IQ256_GATHER` can force the variant for a fresh process.

There is already an NT1-only IQ3_S paired GU helper (`gu_rows_paired_one`), behind `STRATA_IQ256_PAIRED_GU=1`. It loads each Q8_K activation vector once and reuses it for gate and up, but decodes the two weight blocks independently and maintains two accumulator streams. The ordinary GU route runs separate row dots for gate and up. This is an existing opt-in implementation, not a missing kernel or demonstrated improvement. The generic paired GU helper uses an alternate accumulation/reduction path; any test must check the established native/ggml parity and model-level quality gate. Do not promote it based only on a synthetic unit or a component timing.

For IQ4_NL Down, the custom AVX2 routine is selected only when `nt >= mt_min`; default `mt_min` is 2. At NT1, production dispatch goes to GGML. Current source has a custom NT1 row implementation available, but prior source review (R70) found its FP accumulation/reduction order differs from GGML. The generic `STRATA_IQ_MT_MIN=1` changes multiple GU and Down choices and is not a safe isolated switch. Prior R7 reports also rejected a different two-output-row IQ4_NL experiment after decode regressions. Therefore an NT1 Down dispatch change is low priority and needs an exactness-preserving kernel or an explicit numerical/quality requalification; do not revive the rejected row-tile approach.

Known-safe pack metadata receipts (R371 v2) show IQ3_S GU / IQ4_NL Down is present in 9 layers and IQ3_S GU / Q2_0 Down in one layer, among 48. This identifies possible layer-format eligibility only. It does not establish that any selected expert reached CPU in the current request, nor how much service or critical-path time it contributes. The exact CPU-job/type census remains a necessary gate.

## Ranked selective candidates

1. **Re-measure IQ3_S scalar versus gathered decode on the actual 5600X, then adjust only IQ3_S dispatch if the win repeats.** This is the strongest low-risk candidate: both implementations already exist, select only type 21, preserve the same quantized inputs and arithmetic family, and can be compared by existing dispatch control. Upstream issue #26450 records first-person single-core, 100 MB measurements on Intel 13900K: IQ3_S gather improved P-core throughput 5.22 to 9.94 GB/s, while E-core fell 2.29 to 1.73 GB/s; the post describes gather losing on AMD. This is useful evidence that CPU-specific crossover is real and that Intel measurements do not transfer to Ryzen. It is not a Ryzen result or an application result. **Decisive next test:** first require a closed route receipt showing meaningful actual IQ3_S CPU NT1 work; then run existing kernel dispatch parity/bench with forced scalar/gather on pinned 5600X, same exact type-21 blocks, activation bytes, thread/pool settings and alternating arms. Verify all outputs against the accepted reference. Only if the gather component win is repeatable should the unchanged full `bench.sh --long --runs 3` at actual prompt length be used to evaluate end-to-end impact. Keep one candidate dispatch conditional; no generic all-format gather switch.

2. **Treat paired IQ3_S GU as an existing prototype that needs route-relevant validation, not a new kernel to adopt.** At NT1 it removes one activation vector load per block-half across gate/up. Benefit is bounded to load-port/L1 pressure: the same activation is reused immediately by adjacent rows, so this is not evidence of reduced DRAM traffic. Register pressure, table gathers and changed reduction order may offset the saved load. The environment arm is currently opt-in and source-only evidence does not warrant enabling it. **Decisive next test:** after a closed per-format/per-NT route census establishes enough type-21 CPU work, compare paired off/on with fresh processes and identical route/weights, first direct GU correctness and component distributions, inspect generated code for spills, then run the exact unchanged long decode benchmark and quality comparison. Keep the path opt-in unless repeated end-to-end gain and quality gates pass. This re-tests the present prototype; it does not justify adopting a flag from synthetic parity alone.

3. **Do not dispatch IQ4_NL Down NT1 to the present AVX2 routine without an exactness repair and new evidence.** The current routine supports NT1 but default leaves it on GGML because the custom reduction order differs. The type-pair census confirms eligible layers, but the active NT1 production extent remains unmeasured. First require current decode's actual NT1 Down20 jobs and component timing. If Down20 is material, implement an exact-order variant only after separately authorized code work; test every row against GGML and the model quality/greedy-output gates, then compare direct component and unchanged full decode. Otherwise stop. This is a gated follow-up, not a recommendation to set `STRATA_IQ_MT_MIN=1`.

## Other-engine comparison and primary sources

- GGML/llama.cpp registers IQ3_S against `ggml_vec_dot_iq3_s_q8_K` with Q8_K activations; this confirms the fallback's type/activation pairing, not superiority on Ryzen. Upstream source: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c
- The local scalar IQ3_S and vector-gather variants are directly comparable algorithmic alternatives. Upstream llama.cpp issue #26450 documents a first-person AVX2 gather tuning report and hardware-dependent results (13900K P vs E core); it explicitly says AMD behavior differs. Source/discussion: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/26450
- GGML IQ4_NL PR #5590 discusses the lookup-table implementation versus polynomial decoding and includes benchmark context. It is useful for decode-mechanism provenance only; its Ryzen 7950X kernel/model results are not portable to 5600X Strata MoE. https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/5590
- GGML's CPU repack implementation has specialized IQ4_NL GEMV paths, but it is a different packed format/path and no equivalent IQ3_S MoE expert-row fast path was established in this review. Repack source: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/ggml/src/ggml-cpu/repack.h

## Measurement boundaries

Do not infer DRAM bytes from logical expert extents or say CPU is the critical path from job counts alone. A decisive result needs: request/layer/type/NT CPU job incidence; selected kernel/variant; direct GU or Down service distribution; worker/task and wait boundaries; and full request wall/quality under the same route. Keep the model-decode result separate from synthetic throughput and upstream `tg`/quant-dot microbenchmarks. The route ledger's group/extent counts can prioritize the next question but cannot replace these measurements.

## Sources and prior reports consulted

Local reports reviewed for settled scope and rejected paths: R263 AVX2 candidate screen; R294 paired-GU prior evidence/current route; R371 v2 corrected type/byte/NT census and validation plan; R70 IQ4_NL NT1 exact-row candidate contract; R7 IQ4_NL row tile rejection; R213 native CPU roofline/production NT gap; R407 v2 capacity correction; R405 v2 phase lease safety; R408 residual transport precision. The R405/R407/R408 source work is orthogonal to CPU decode kernels. No settled scalar/tensor-count claims are repeated here beyond the format/eligibility needed to rank these candidate gates.

Report writer: source researcher. No source, test, model, GPU, service, build, profiler, process or Git state changed.
